one_line: An urban craft specialist of the Gangetic plain, firing lustrous fine ceramics for early historic elites.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s, lean and wiry from manual work, with slightly broad shoulders and strong forearms.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown north Indian complexion, straight nose, high cheekbones, a light stubble beard and faint kiln-scorch marks on the cheeks; eyes are large, dark and alert with a focused, craftsman’s gaze and a calm default expression.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair tied back in a short, neat topknot at the crown with a simple brown cotton cord, sides and back trimmed to ear length, no turban or cap.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length, undyed off‑white cotton dhoti wrapped tightly around the waist and brought between the legs in a simple kosha‑style tuck, a lightweight mid‑brown cotton uttariya shawl draped over both shoulders and hanging to mid‑thigh, and a fitted, plain, short‑sleeved off‑white cotton angarkha-style upper garment tied at the right side; on his feet are simple dark brown leather sandals, and around his waist a narrow red woven cloth belt; a thin bronze bangle on his right wrist and a small copper amulet on a black thread at his neck add modest ornament, while his hands and forearms show faint grayish-black kiln dust and clay stains.
appearance.signature: A shallow, lustrous Northern Black Polished Ware bowl in his left hand, mirror‑dark on the exterior with a subtle graphite sheen and reddish‑brown core at a chipped rim, and in his right hand a smooth wooden potter’s rib tool, both handled carefully like prized instruments.

ref_desc: A lean late‑20s north Indian potter with medium‑brown skin, black hair in a short topknot, calm dark eyes, off‑white dhoti and angarkha, mid‑brown shawl, red belt, bronze bangle, sandals, holding a glossy black NBPW bowl and a wooden potter’s tool.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of a historically grounded early historic north Indian potter: a lean late‑20s man with medium‑brown complexion, oval face, straight nose, light stubble, faint kiln‑smudge marks and large calm dark eyes; his thick black hair is tied in a short neat topknot at the crown with a brown cord, the sides and back cut to ear length, with no headgear. Dress him in an off‑white cotton knee‑length dhoti wrapped snugly with a simple between‑the‑legs tuck, a plain off‑white short‑sleeved angarkha‑style upper garment tied on the right side, and a lightweight mid‑brown cotton shawl (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and hanging to mid‑thigh; cinch his waist with a narrow brick‑red woven cloth belt. Put simple dark brown leather sandals on his feet, a thin bronze bangle on his right wrist and a small copper amulet pendant on a black thread at his neck, and show subtle gray‑black clay and soot stains on his hands and forearms. In his left hand he gently displays a shallow Northern Black Polished Ware bowl with a deep graphite‑black, mirror‑like exterior sheen and a hint of reddish‑brown at a tiny chip on the rim, while in his right hand he holds a smooth wooden potter’s rib tool; keep the colour palette to off‑white, mid‑brown, dark brown, brick red and graphite black, and present him front‑facing in a neutral, steady pose so every costume and facial detail is clearly visible.
